name: gate
wording: A point at a handover where the work stops for the operator's sign-off: a story's read-back, held by the architect; a story's plan read-back, held by the lead, which a task with no story skips unless the operator calls it; a pull request the operator reviews, held by the lead before it merges; release; a fork that is irreversible, about value or beyond the architect's competence; and any point the operator calls, stop included. A gate is held in the session of the party whose handover it is, which ends its turn there, its reply ending with the sign-off it waits on, until the operator answers; the operator joins that session. The party that delegated the work takes no part in it: of what passes there, nothing reaches its own context by any route, a summary it later reads included, beyond the fact that the work waits on the operator, and then the result; a record it never reads is not learning. Pushing a branch or opening a pull request is never a gate, and between gates the agents work without checking in.
reason: Realizing it on a harness raised whether 'learns only' binds the results the delegating party is handed or also what the harness keeps and later summarizes for it. It binds whatever reaches that party's own context, by any route; and the delegating party does not join a gate held for the operator, so technical colour never passes through it.
